name.text: Evaluating trigonometric expressions with angles in radians

questiontext.text:
Find the exact value of

\[ [[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] [[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right). \]

(a) Find the exact value of \([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right)\).

\([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prta]]

(b) Find the exact value of \([[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right)\).

\([[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right) = \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prtb]]

(c) Hence find the exact value of \([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] [[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right)\).

\([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] [[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right) = \) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prtc]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Both angles are special angles. Change each one to degrees, use the exact values from the special triangles, then combine them.

(a) The first term

Step 1: change the angle to degrees. Since \(\pi \text{ radians} = 180^\circ\), \({@A1@} = \dfrac{180^\circ}{ {@d1@} } = {@dg1@}^\circ\).

Step 2: use the exact value. \([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) = [[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]] {@dg1@}^\circ = {@v1@}\).

(b) The second term

Step 1: change the angle to degrees. \({@A2@} = \dfrac{180^\circ}{ {@d2@} } = {@dg2@}^\circ\).

Step 2: use the exact value. \([[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right) = [[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]] {@dg2@}^\circ = {@v2@}\).

These come from the table of exact values:

\(\theta\)\(\dfrac{\pi}{6} = 30^\circ\)\(\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 45^\circ\)\(\dfrac{\pi}{3} = 60^\circ\)\(\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 90^\circ\)
\(\sin\theta\)\(\dfrac{1}{2}\)\(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\)\(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)\(1\)
\(\cos\theta\)\(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)\(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\)\(\dfrac{1}{2}\)\(0\)
\(\tan\theta\)\(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\)\(1\)\(\sqrt{3}\)undefined

(c) Combining the terms

Step 3: substitute the values and simplify.

\[ [[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] [[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right) = {@v1@} [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] {@v2@} = {@ta@}. \]

Final answer: \([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f1=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A1@}\right) [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] [[if test="is(f2=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(f2=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left({@A2@}\right) = {@ta@}\).
